extracted.intended_audience: public relations and communications writing teachers; AEJMC Public Relations Division members; communications program administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and recommended feature set for applying computer-assisted instruction to teaching public relations/journalistic writing, including lab-based basic course modules and an interactive 'Writer's Advisor' to assist students during composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic mechanics coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should teach and reinforce the mechanics of grammar, punctuation, spelling, abbreviation, capitalization, word compounding, titles and other stylebook forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core Basic Course Program topics to be offered in a Communications Computer Center; instruction may be brief review but the machine should drill and test until mastery is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular course design
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Basic Course Program (module) should be subdivided into several smaller units to aid programming, repetition and testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submodules allow incremental testing and remediation; incorrect responses trigger additional instruction and retesting; completion of segments leads to non-record practice tests and then to a formal recorded overall test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery threshold and testing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must train and test until they score at least 90 percent correct on the module record test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs may permit skipping instruction and going directly to record tests, but this may produce poor recorded grades; non-record (practice) tests are available and formal tests are randomly drawn questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-keeping and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: A record is kept of the student's name and grades on each final test completed in a program module; no other record of a student's work will be retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive program managers document completed segments and scores and resume sessions where the student left off; teachers may inspect student computer time and record test scores to assist instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom concept prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: Concepts should be taught in classroom sessions prior to use of the computer center; the machine programs concentrate on reinforcement rather than primary concept transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students unable to demonstrate basic understanding in class should be referred for remedial English per school procedures rather than relying on the center as primary instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications Computer Center as laboratory
rubrics_metrics.description: A departmental Communications Computer Center should serve as a laboratory where students train at video display terminals as part of writing courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers should allow assigned time and additional time on request, track student progress, and provide standardized Basic Course Programs across participating members (e.g., using a common stylebook like AP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality and style conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic Course Programs can be made universally applicable if participating members adopt the same style conventions (for example, the Associated Press Stylebook).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizing on a particular stylebook facilitates widely usable programs and program portability across institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program segmentation (two-segment model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-segment requirement: Segment One — Basic Course Programs for the Communications Computer Center; Segment Two — the Writer's Advisor, an interactive system used while the student writes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the two segments as complementary packages with different design goals: the Basic Course is axiomatic and mastery-focused; the Writer's Advisor is advisory and used in-process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer's Advisor: readability measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Writer's Advisor should calculate readability (grade level) using machine measures that correlate with standard Flesch and Cloze formulas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readability is generally computed from average word and sentence length and gives the writer a consistent measure of reader comprehension ease; useful for tailoring copy to audience grade levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer's Advisor: sentence and word length analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should analyze sentence and word length, flagging long sentences and computing averages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For broadcast copy and narrow newspaper columns, short words and short sentences are recommended; some programs call attention to sentences over a set threshold (e.g., 20 words) and count long vs. short sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer's Advisor: quotation detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs may detect presence or absence of quotation marks and remind the writer if none are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotations often enliven copy; the Advisor can prompt writers to consider including quotes if none are found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer's Advisor: keyword and personalization counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should count occurrences of key words and pronouns (e.g., 'you') to inform tone, emphasis, and personalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive use of 'you' implies informal, conversational copy; keyword counts help ensure required terms appear sufficiently often.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer's Advisor: passive voice detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should search for verbs that indicate passive voice and report the proportion of passive constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program might print messages like 'You used the passive verb form 50 percent of the time in this passage' and cite the verb instances, reminding that active verbs yield more active copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation and spelling routines (advisory, not foolproof)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spellcheck and punctuation routines should highlight probable errors and suggest corrections, but be presented as advisory because they are not infallible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper names or unusual forms may trigger false positives; the writer should be allowed to accept or reject suggested corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cliché detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs (e.g., CLICHE) should search for trite expressions and highlight them for the writer to retain or remove.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of caught clichés and let writers decide whether to revise for originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idiom correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs (e.g., IDIOM) should flag nonstandard or incorrect idioms and advise correct usage with sentence references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: flagging 'conform with the rules' and advising 'conform to the rules,' with the sentence number cited for easy revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs (e.g., CONCISE) should suggest shorter replacements for wordy phrases and flag filler phrases to be eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide direct replacements such as 'at all times' -> 'always', and list common verbose phrases recommended for elimination ('all things considered', 'for all intents and purposes').

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer's Advisor advisory role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Writer's Advisor routines are advisory rather than axiomatic, intended to assist the writer while they work and free the teacher to focus on higher-order writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions should be presented as recommendations the writer may use or ignore; mastery of Advisor routines is not critical in the same way as Basic Course modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program behavioral flow (interaction model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should support sign-on, session continuity, instructor-visible progress messages, choices to take instruction or test, and branching based on responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample interaction includes greeting, reminding of prior module completions, offering to skip to tests, presenting short instructional content, prompting for answers, and responding with corrective explanations when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remediation and referral policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Students unable to demonstrate basic understanding prior to center use should be referred for remedial English according to school procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The center is for reinforcement after classroom concept mastery; rare cases of fundamental deficiency should follow institutional remediation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization and procurement recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Relations Division of AEJMC should form committees to state requirements to the computer industry for interactive terminals and programs, gain AEJMC endorsement, and make requirements available to interested companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agreed requirement will define a significant market and spur industry to propose effective and economical CAI packages; committees should solicit member input and include technical expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardware/terminal standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration should be given to long-term requirements for standardized interactive terminals and student terminals to support CAI programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizing terminals and program interfaces will help shape comprehensive student interactive computer requirements and ease program deployment across institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation and documented effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should be evaluated empirically (testing CAI vs. tutoring/self-study) and documented; prior studies (e.g., JSTYLE, LARS) indicate CAI can substitute effectively for instructor tutoring in basic language skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experimental testing results and bibliography to demonstrate feasibility and guide program improvements; use proven readability and error-detection approaches where available.
